text:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — high tail latency detected for hosted inference pool 'hostpool-prod' (p95 spike). Pager sent to @alex_oncall. Severity: P2 -> escalated on-call.

alex_oncall: ack. I'm looking. Observed p50 stable, p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 2.8s across multiple routes. Customers routing through dedicated also unaffected.

maya_sre: joining. Any recent infra changes reported? kernel or kube node updates?

jordan_runtime: quick note — we rolled a kernel patch to 5.15.0-102 last night on 50% of nodes for spectre backport. Can verify which hosts are in the hot path.

alex_oncall: running live sampling on the affected hosts. Attaching top-like snapshot and perf counters.

alex_oncall: ```
# top snapshot (abridged)
PID USER     PR  NI    VIRT    RES  %CPU %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
2301 redruu  20   0  23.4g  1.1g  73.5  4.2  12:13.45 runtime-worker
2278 redruu  20   0  16.2g  512m  12.3  2.0   1:02.11 model-server
```

alex_oncall: perf stat short-run (2s window):
```
cycles: 8.2G
context-switches: 1.2M
cpu-migrations: 48k
page-faults: 94k
```

priya_prod: customer ops reporting 5-10s spikes for 3 enterprise customers, and ~20% request failure due to client timeouts. We already routed some traffic to fallback small model.

maya_sre: page-faults high -> could indicate kernel-level paging or IO contention. Are these nodes under memory pressure or using host swapping? Check vmstat and dmesg for OOM or excessive swapping.

alex_oncall: vmstat shows high si/so around the p95 window; free memory not exhausted but reclaim thrashing possible. dmesg has no OOM kills but correlates with a flurry of anon page reclaim messages.

jordan_runtime: can we get a trace span sample for a slow request? Need to see where time is spent (runtime kernel syscalls vs user compute). If it's blocking on page faults we'll see high time in 'wait' spans.

alex_oncall: pasting one sampled trace (redacted) — timestamped timeline lines only:
```
[00:00.000] recv request
[00:00.012] load tokenizer shards (disk mmap)
[00:00.300] first token gen
[00:01.900] stall - 1.6s blocking on page fault (madvise/mmap)
[00:02.050] resume, kv cache apply
[00:02.100] send response
```

ben_support: customer impact notes: three enterprise lanes reported timeouts, one support ticket created with high priority. Notified account execs.

maya_sre: hypothesis list (in-thread):
- H1: Kernel change (5.15.0-102) regressed anon page reclaim behavior under our memory access pattern -> more blocking page faults for cold mmaps.
- H2: Batching change in runtime that increased large working set accesses, causing more demand paging at tail.
- H3: Underlying storage (NFS/remote) regression causing mmap-backed tokenizer loads to block.

jordan_runtime: quick check — our recent batching config change increased prefetch window for tokenizer shards. Reverting that should reduce cold page faulting. Rolling a canary revert to 10% now.

alex_oncall: mitigation enacted: 1) scaled hostpool-prod +25% nodes (to reduce per-node working set), 2) traffic steering: route long-tail customers to fallback model, 3) reverted batching canary (jordan), 4) collecting full perf + ftrace for 5 minutes. Early metrics: p95 trending down to ~620ms but still noisy.

priya_prod: customers notified: initial incident message + mitigation steps. Will update status page with ETA for full resolution.

maya_sre: next data to gather:
- ftrace showing blocked_on_page_fault stacks (please paste kernel stack samples)
- vmstat / slabinfo around spike windows
- compare affected nodes with kernel version to control group
- SSD/FS metrics for mmap-backed files

alex_oncall: pushing collection bundle to share link: https://internal.redwood/incoming/trace-bundles/1767774444 . Uploaded ftrace, perf, vmstat, dmesg. Granting access to the SRE and runtime leads.

jordan_runtime: initial diff shows increased anonvms pressure from prefetch. Revert canary looks good; the 10% revert hosts show no page-fault burst. Will schedule full revert for next 5 minutes if stable.

ben_support: logging follow-ups: ticket #INC-1749 created per-customer with timeline and mitigation notes.

maya_sre: long-form RCA hypotheses to test post-incident:
- Reproduce with synthetic workload: cold tokenizer loads + batching prefetch on kernel 5.15.0-102 vs 5.15.0-100.
- Run perf counters for page-fault latency distribution.
- Coordinate with infra to evaluate kernel patch changelog for mm/anon reclaim changes.

alex_oncall: moving to monitoring mode. Will update thread when p95 sustained < 300ms for 15m. Assigning owner for RCA: @maya_sre (infra), @jordan_runtime (runtime). @priya_prod will handle customer comms. Closing pager for on-call but keeping incident open.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation in place, status: recovering. Logged event to incident timeline.
